newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola's Catoca mine likely to produce from May.
newsitem.headline: Angola's Catoca mine likely to produce from May.

text.p: Angola's only operating kimberlite mine is likely to begin producing diamonds within two months, an official for Brazil's Odebrecht company said on Friday.
"We see no reason why Catoca should not begin producing by May," Otacilio Carvalho, Odebrecht's director of operations for southern Africa, told Reuters.
"We have great hopes that this project is going to turn out well for us. We have been involved in this since 1995 and are very much looking forward to seeing production start," he added.
The Catoca mine is located in Angola's northeastern Lunda Sul province and is believed to be one of the world's largest kimberlite deposits.
Odebrecht has a 20 percent share in the mine together with Angola's state diamond company Endiama and Russia's Almazy Rossii-Sakha (ARS) diamond monopoly which both hold 40 percent.
Carvalho said preliminary studies showed that Catoca is likely to produce around six million carats in the first nine years.
Angola produces between $700 million and $1 billion in diamonds annually but because of the country's two-decade-long civil war its vast kimberlite reserves have mostly remained untouched.
South Africa's Bureau of Mineral and Energy Affairs figures show that Angola produced 2.9 million carats in 1995.
The former rebel UNITA movement controls most of Angola's diamond areas around the Cuango river valley -- an area which alone generates around a million carats annually.
The government and the former rebels, who signed a peace accord in 1994 to end the civil war, are currently in talks to carve up the diamond area.
Most diamonds produced in Angola are alluvial deposits.
There are an estimated 630 kimberlite pipes in Angola, at least 300 of them with grades better than .04 carats per cubic metre.
